text: Where is the URL class defined in yarl?
rationale: The public URL type is a __slots__ class declared at yarl/_url.py:356 (`class URL`) with the full RFC 3986 grammar in its leading comment block; yarl/__init__.py re-exports it, and the name resolves to exactly one class in the graph.

text: Where is the function that parses an unencoded URL string into a URL object?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:226 defines the lru_cache-decorated encode_url ('Parse unencoded URL') that URL.__new__ dispatches to for str inputs (yarl/_url.py:445).

text: Where is the function that parses an already-encoded URL string without re-quoting?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:292 defines the lru_cache-decorated pre_encoded_url ('Parse pre-encoded URL'); URL.__new__ routes encoded=True str inputs to it (yarl/_url.py:445).

text: Where is split_url defined, the function that breaks a URL string into scheme, netloc, path, query and fragment?
rationale: yarl/_parse.py:24 defines split_url ('Split URL into parts'), adapted from urllib.parse.urlsplit with WHATWG leading-C0 stripping and IPv6 bracket validation.

text: Where is make_netloc defined, the helper that reassembles user:password@host:port?
rationale: yarl/_parse.py:188 defines make_netloc ('Make netloc from parts'), used by every code path that rebuilds an authority string.

text: Where is split_netloc defined, the function that splits a netloc into username, password, host and port?
rationale: yarl/_parse.py:131 defines split_netloc ('Split netloc into username, password, host and port'), including the bracketed-IPv6 branch and 0-65535 port validation.

text: Where is the host encoder _encode_host defined?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:1646 defines _encode_host ('Encode host part of URL') with the IP-address fast path, NOT_REG_NAME validation and the IDNA branch.

text: Where is normalize_path defined, the function that removes '.' and '..' segments from a path?
rationale: yarl/_path.py:31 defines normalize_path ('Drop . and .. from str path'), preserving the leading '/' per RFC 3986 sections 5.2.4 and 6.2.2.3 as its comment notes.

text: Where is normalize_path_segments defined, the segment-level dot-removal helper?
rationale: yarl/_path.py:7 defines normalize_path_segments ('Drop . and .. from a sequence of str segments'); normalize_path delegates to it and _make_child calls it for absolute URLs.

text: Where is the pure-Python _Quoter class that percent-encodes URL components?
rationale: yarl/_quoting_py.py:22 defines _Quoter, the byte-level state machine honoring safe/protected/qs/requote flags; yarl/_quoting.py imports it as the fallback backend when the Cython extension is absent.

text: Where is the _Unquoter class that decodes percent-encoded URL components?
rationale: yarl/_quoting_py.py:121 defines _Unquoter with the incremental UTF-8 decoder handling ignore/unsafe/qs/plus modes; yarl/_quoting.py imports it alongside _Quoter.

text: Where is human_quote defined, the helper that escapes unsafe characters for human-readable output?
rationale: yarl/_quoters.py:24 defines human_quote, which percent-escapes '%' plus a caller-chosen unsafe set and falls back to urllib quote for unprintables; URL.human_repr is its only caller.

text: Where is get_str_query defined, the entry point that serializes query arguments into a query string?
rationale: yarl/_query.py:85 defines get_str_query ('Return a query string from supported args'), dispatching on dict/str/Mapping/Sequence inputs.

text: Where is query_var defined, the function that converts a single query value to a string?
rationale: yarl/_query.py:18 defines query_var ('Convert a query variable to a string') with the int fast path, float inf/nan rejection and the SupportsInt branch.

text: Where is query_to_pairs defined, the parser that splits a query string into key/value pairs?
rationale: yarl/_parse.py:221 defines query_to_pairs ('Parse a query given as a string argument'), an urllib.parse.parse_qsl-shaped splitter using UNQUOTER_PLUS.

text: Where is unsplit_result defined, the inverse of split_url that renders components back into a string?
rationale: yarl/_parse.py:171 defines unsplit_result ('Unsplit a URL without any normalization'); URL.__str__ and URL.human_repr both end with it.

text: Where is URL.with_name defined, the method that replaces the last path segment?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:1426 defines URL.with_name ('Return a new URL with name (last part of path) replaced'), rejecting slash-bearing and dot names.

text: Where is __str__ defined on the URL class?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:564 defines URL.__str__ (default-port normalization then unsplit_result); the only other __str__ in the snapshot is the repr helper class in tests/test_update_query.py used to assert query-string concatenation.

text: Which functions call make_netloc to assemble an authority string?
rationale: All 11 precise caller edges live in yarl/_url.py: the parser path encode_url, the rendering paths __str__/human_repr/authority, the builder URL.build, and the with_user/with_password/with_host/with_port mutators rebuild netloc through it.

text: Who calls split_netloc to decompose an authority into user, password, host and port?
rationale: Precise callers: encode_url for complex netlocs (yarl/_url.py:236), URL.build when an authority= argument is given (yarl/_url.py:525), and _cache_netloc which fills the per-instance cache (yarl/_url.py:664).

text: Who calls split_url when turning a URL string into parts?
rationale: Exactly the two cached constructors call it: encode_url (yarl/_url.py:230) and pre_encoded_url (yarl/_url.py:295).

text: Which code paths call normalize_path to collapse dot segments?
rationale: Callers span parse (encode_url, yarl/_url.py:268), build (URL.build, yarl/_url.py:543), mutation (with_path, yarl/_url.py:1264), joining (URL.join, yarl/_url.py:1545) and the direct unit test tests/test_normalize_path.py:test_normalize_path.

text: Who calls get_str_query to build a query string from arguments?
rationale: The three query-mutation methods call it: URL.build (yarl/_url.py:506), with_query (yarl/_url.py:1291) and extend_query (yarl/_url.py:1312).

text: Which functions call query_var to coerce a query value to a string?
rationale: Both list comprehensions in yarl/_query.py route non-str values through query_var: get_str_query_from_sequence_iterable (line 57) and get_str_query_from_iterable (line 80).

text: Who calls human_quote while rendering a human-readable URL?
rationale: URL.human_repr is the only caller, six call sites in one body (yarl/_url.py:1563-1576) escaping user, password, host path components, query keys/values and fragment.

text: Who calls query_to_pairs to parse an existing query string?
rationale: The cached property _parsed_query (yarl/_url.py:973) and update_query's str branch (yarl/_url.py:1366) both parse pair lists from raw query strings.

text: Who calls normalize_path_segments to resolve dot segments on a segment list?
rationale: normalize_path splits and delegates (yarl/_path.py:41) and URL._make_child normalizes appended segments for absolute URLs (yarl/_url.py:1147).

text: Who calls unsplit_result to serialize URL components back to a string?
rationale: The two rendering paths end in it: URL.__str__ (yarl/_url.py:578) and URL.human_repr (yarl/_url.py:1580).

text: Which accessors trigger _cache_netloc to populate the netloc cache?
rationale: The four raw netloc accessors call it on miss: raw_user and raw_password (yarl/_url.py:784/805), raw_host (yarl/_url.py:830) and explicit_port (yarl/_url.py:936).

text: Which tests exercise URL.with_name?
rationale: 17 precise call sites across tests/test_url.py, tests/test_url_parsing.py and tests/test_url_benchmarks.py, led by test_with_name and the relative-path variants.

text: Which tests call URL.with_host?
rationale: 13 call sites, concentrated in tests/test_url_update_netloc.py (with one benchmark helper in tests/test_url_benchmarks.py), led by test_with_host itself.

text: Which tests call URL.with_suffix?
rationale: 20 call sites across tests/test_url.py and tests/test_url_parsing.py, led by test_with_suffix plus the dot/empty edge cases.

text: Which tests exercise URL.build?
rationale: 82 precise call sites across tests/test_url_build.py (the dedicated builder suite, led by test_build_simple), tests/test_url.py, tests/test_url_parsing.py and tests/test_url_benchmarks.py.

text: Which tests call URL.join?
rationale: tests/test_url.py carries the join suite: test_join plus the RFC 3986 5.2.4 matrices test_join_from_rfc_3986_normal/abnormal and the CPython-parity test_join_cpython_urljoin; more call sites live in tests/test_url_benchmarks.py.

text: Who calls _encode_relative_scheme_colon to protect relative paths from scheme-shaped colons?
rationale: Every constructor/render path that can produce a scheme-less path calls it: encode_url (yarl/_url.py:270), URL.build (yarl/_url.py:552), build_pre_encoded_url (line 327), from_parts_uncached (line 343) and human_repr (line 1571).

text: Which tests call URL.without_query_params?
rationale: The dedicated pair in tests/test_url_query.py: test_without_query_params and test_skip_dropping_query_params.

text: Which tests exercise URL.is_default_port?
rationale: Seven distinct call sites: six port-semantics tests in tests/test_url.py (default port, non-default port, no port, relative URL, unknown scheme, port zero) plus benchmark helpers in tests/test_url_benchmarks.py.

text: Who calls _idna_encode when encoding a host?
rationale: _encode_host's non-ASCII branch (yarl/_url.py:1717) and the sweep test tests/test_url.py:test_idna_collapses that pins default-ignorable coverage.

text: What breaks if make_netloc changes its netloc assembly rules?
rationale: Impact fans out through every constructor: encode_url at depth 0, URL.__new__ at 1, pre_encoded_url/build_pre_encoded_url at 2, URL.build at 3 and the builder tests at 4 (181 impacted symbols total) - all rebuild an authority through make_netloc (yarl/_parse.py:188).

text: What is the blast radius of changing _encode_host?
rationale: Callers at depth 0 are encode_url, build and with_host; the closure then reaches URL.__new__ and pre_encoded_url, i.e. every path that accepts or replaces a host goes through yarl/_url.py:1646 (118 impacted symbols).

text: What breaks if split_url's parsing rules change?
rationale: Both cached constructors sit directly upstream (encode_url, pre_encoded_url at depth 0) and URL.__new__ one hop above them (yarl/_url.py:230/295/445); 103 impacted symbols.

text: What breaks if query_to_pairs changes how query strings are split into pairs?
rationale: Exactly two direct consumers, both in yarl/_url.py: the _parsed_query cached property feeding URL.query (line 973) and update_query's str branch (line 1366).

text: What breaks if from_parts_uncached changes how URLs are constructed from parts?
rationale: The three query mutators build their result through it (with_query, update_query, extend_query at depth 0; yarl/_url.py:1292/1388/1320).

text: What breaks if get_str_query changes its serialization rules?
rationale: Depth-0 impact: URL.build plus with_query and extend_query; the closure then reaches the whole builder test suite (85 impacted symbols, yarl/_query.py:85).

text: What breaks if query_var starts rejecting more query value types?
rationale: get_str_query_from_sequence_iterable at depth 0, get_str_query at 1, URL.build at 2, and builder tests like test_build_simple at 3 (93 impacted symbols; yarl/_query.py:18).

text: What breaks if human_quote changes its escaping rules?
rationale: URL.human_repr is the sole in-package caller (depth 0); the human-repr tests break at depth 1, including test_human_repr and the scheme-confusion regression test_human_repr_does_not_introduce_scheme (yarl/_quoters.py:24).

text: What breaks if normalize_path changes how dot segments are resolved?
rationale: Direct callers encode_url, join, with_path, build and the unit test test_normalize_path; the closure above encode_url/build reaches 234 impacted symbols (yarl/_path.py:31).

text: What breaks if unsplit_result changes how URLs render back to strings?
rationale: URL.__str__ and URL.human_repr at depth 0, then every test asserting rendered output, e.g. test_human_repr at depth 1 (21 impacted symbols; yarl/_parse.py:171).

text: Trace the code path from parsing an unencoded URL string to a cached URL object.
rationale: trace_flow from encode_url: split_url (yarl/_parse.py) then _check_netloc on the non-ASCII branch, split_netloc for complex netlocs, _encode_host with _idna_encode, make_netloc to reassemble, normalize_path/normalize_path_segments for dotted paths, _encode_relative_scheme_colon for scheme-less paths, and URL.__new__ upstream.

text: Trace the flow of URL.build when constructing a URL from components with a query.
rationale: From URL.build (yarl/_url.py:465): encoded=True goes to build_pre_encoded_url; the query= argument is serialized by get_str_query into get_str_query_from_iterable / get_str_query_from_sequence_iterable with query_var coercion, and the host leg runs through _encode_host, split_url and make_netloc.

text: Trace the flow of update_query merging new parameters into an existing query string.
rationale: From update_query (yarl/_url.py:1330): the existing query is parsed by query_to_pairs via _parsed_query, merged into a MultiDict, re-serialized by get_str_query_from_sequence_iterable or get_str_query_from_iterable (query_var for non-str values), and the result URL is built by from_parts_uncached.

text: Trace the flow of with_query replacing the query part of a URL.
rationale: From with_query (yarl/_url.py:1277): arguments are serialized via get_str_query (iterable/sequence-iterable branches with query_var), and the new URL is assembled by from_parts_uncached keeping scheme/netloc/path/fragment.

text: Trace the flow of human_repr producing a decoded human-readable URL string.
rationale: From human_repr (yarl/_url.py:1561): every component passes through human_quote (yarl/_quoters.py), relative paths are re-protected by _encode_relative_scheme_colon, and the authority/path are reassembled via make_netloc and unsplit_result.

text: Trace the flow of URL.join resolving a relative reference against a base URL.
rationale: From join (yarl/_url.py:1505): the merged path is normalized by normalize_path which delegates to normalize_path_segments (both in yarl/_path.py) when the merged path contains dots; the result is rebuilt from parts.

text: Trace the flow of joinpath appending path segments to a URL.
rationale: From joinpath (yarl/_url.py:1557) into _make_child, which quotes each appended segment, and resolves dots through normalize_path_segments (reached via normalize_path) before rebuilding the URL.

text: Trace the flow of reading url.host for an internationalized domain.
rationale: The host cached property (yarl/_url.py:834) returns raw hosts verbatim when they look like IPs and otherwise decodes via _idna_decode (yarl/_url.py:1630), which tries idna and falls back to the stdlib codec.

text: Trace the flow of encoding a host during URL construction.
rationale: From _encode_host (yarl/_url.py:1646): IP-shaped hosts take the ip_address fast path; non-ASCII reg-names go through _idna_encode (yarl/_url.py:1638) after the default-ignorable rejection.

text: Trace the flow of extend_query appending parameters to the existing query string.
rationale: From extend_query (yarl/_url.py:1302): new parameters are serialized by get_str_query (with query_var coercion in the iterable branches) and joined onto the existing encoded query before from_parts_uncached rebuilds the URL.

text: How does yarl percent-encode and decode URL components?
rationale: yarl/_quoting_py.py implements the byte-level _Quoter/_Unquoter state machines (safe/protected/qs/requote flags); yarl/_quoters.py configures the per-component instances (QUOTER, PATH_QUOTER, QUERY_QUOTER, FRAGMENT_QUOTER and the unquoters) that the rest of the package calls.

text: What is the difference between the raw_ accessors and the decoded accessors on URL?
rationale: yarl/_url.py pairs each decoded cached_property with a raw_ twin: raw_path returns self._path verbatim while path runs PATH_UNQUOTER (lines 940-955); the same pairing holds for raw_query_string/query_string (QS_UNQUOTER), raw_fragment/fragment (UNQUOTER), raw_user/user and raw_password/password.

text: How does yarl handle internationalized domain names?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:_encode_host lowercases ASCII hosts, rejects non-reg-name characters via NOT_REG_NAME, and routes non-ASCII through _idna_encode (idna with uts46=True, stdlib fallback); reading back goes through _idna_decode, each under lru_cache.

text: How does yarl handle IPv6 literals and RFC 6874 zone identifiers in hosts?
rationale: Bracket handling lives in yarl/_parse.py:split_url (bracket validation) and split_netloc (bracketed hostinfo split); yarl/_url.py:_encode_host spells the zone separator as %25 and validates zone characters, while host_subcomponent and host_port_subcomponent re-add brackets on read-back.

text: How are default ports per scheme handled and normalized?
rationale: The DEFAULT_PORTS map in yarl/_url.py drives everything: URL.build and build_pre_encoded_url drop a port equal to the scheme default, __str__ omits it from rendering, port substitutes it on read, and is_default_port/host_port_subcomponent expose the semantics.

text: How are '.' and '..' dot segments removed from URL paths?
rationale: yarl/_path.py:normalize_path_segments implements RFC 3986 5.2.4-style resolution over a segment list (popping on .., skipping ., keeping the trailing empty segment); normalize_path wraps it for strings; URL._make_child applies it when appending segments to absolute URLs.

text: How does yarl build a query string from mappings, sequences and keyword arguments?
rationale: yarl/_query.py:get_str_query dispatches on the input shape - dicts/Mappings go to get_str_query_from_sequence_iterable (values may be lists/tuples), pair sequences to get_str_query_from_iterable, and every non-str value passes through query_var which supports str/int/float/SupportsInt.

text: How does URL parsing split a URL string into its five components?
rationale: yarl/_parse.py:split_url is the single splitter (scheme detection, // authority extraction with delimiter scan, fragment then query partition, NFKC netloc check via _check_netloc); encode_url and pre_encoded_url call it and cache the resulting tuple.

text: How is the authority (netloc) assembled from user, password, host and port?
rationale: yarl/_parse.py:make_netloc is the assembler (optional user:password@ prefix, port suffix, optional re-quoting of credentials); yarl/_url.py:authority decodes and reassembles on read-back, and _cache_netloc caches the split of self._netloc.

text: What caching does yarl apply and how is it managed?
rationale: yarl/_url.py wraps encode_url, pre_encoded_url, from_parts_uncached (as from_parts), _idna_encode/_idna_decode and _encode_host in lru_cache; cache_clear/cache_info/cache_configure (with the CacheInfo TypedDict) are the management surface exercised by tests/test_cache.py.

text: URL is immutable - how do the with_* methods produce modified copies?
rationale: Every mutator in yarl/_url.py ends in from_parts_uncached (the lru-cached from_parts constructor) with substituted components: with_query/update_query/extend_query swap the query, with_user/with_password/with_host/with_port rebuild the netloc, with_path/with_name/with_suffix replace path parts, join merges references.

text: How is pickling of URL objects supported?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:__getstate__ returns a plain tuple (with a comment explaining the SplitResult pickling pitfall on Python 3.15+) and __setstate__ accepts both the current tuple shape and legacy dict/SplitResult pickles; tests/test_pickle.py pins the behavior.

text: How are URL objects compared and hashed?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:__eq__ compares the five raw components (normalizing an empty path to '/' when a netloc is present) and __hash__ caches a hash of the same tuple, so equal URLs hash equal and encoded forms matter; tests/test_url_cmp_and_hash.py pins it.

text: How does a URL object render itself back to a string?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:__str__ applies default-port normalization then delegates to yarl/_parse.py:unsplit_result; __bytes__ is the ASCII encoding of the same string.

text: What produces the human-readable representation of a URL and how does it differ from str()?
rationale: URL.human_repr (yarl/_url.py:1561) decodes components and escapes delimiters per component via human_quote (yarl/_quoters.py), unlike __str__ which renders the encoded form; tests/test_url.py carries the dedicated test_human_repr suite.

text: How are path segments and the parent path accessed on a URL?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:raw_parts splits the encoded path (keeping the leading '/' for absolute URLs), parts decodes each segment through UNQUOTER, parent drops the last segment via from_parts, and name/raw_name expose the final segment.

text: How are file suffixes of the last path segment computed and replaced?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:raw_suffix/raw_suffixes split the encoded name on dots, suffix/suffixes decode them, and with_suffix replaces the extension (rejecting malformed suffixes and empty names).

text: How does yarl distinguish absolute from relative URLs?
rationale: yarl/_url.py: absolute (cached_property) tests a non-empty netloc, is_absolute() wraps it, relative() strips scheme/authority (rejecting relative inputs), and origin/_origin reduce an absolute URL to scheme+host+port.

text: How does URL.join implement RFC 3986 reference resolution?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:join merges scheme/netloc from the base, resolves the relative path (absolute, trailing-slash and last-segment replacement cases), normalizes dots via yarl/_path.py:normalize_path, and carries query/fragment only when the reference provides them.

text: What validation protects against host confusion and SSRF-style netloc tricks?
rationale: Three layers: yarl/_parse.py:split_url rejects unbalanced/misplaced IPv6 brackets and text after ']', _check_netloc rejects NFKC-normalizing netlocs (the \u2100 'a/c' trick), and yarl/_url.py:_encode_host rejects non-reg-name characters and default-ignorable code points that IDNA would silently delete.

text: How does yarl integrate with pydantic for URL validation and serialization?
rationale: yarl/_url.py defines __get_pydantic_core_schema__ (chain/union schemas with a str validator and plain str serializer) and __get_pydantic_json_schema__ (type string, format uri), guarded by the HAS_PYDANTIC probe so the import stays lazy.

text: How is subclassing of URL prevented?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:__init_subclass__ raises TypeError for any subclass ('Inheriting a class ... from URL is forbidden'), keeping the __slots__ layout and caching assumptions intact.

text: What operator overloads does URL provide?
rationale: yarl/_url.py: __truediv__ (url / 'segment') appends a path segment via _make_child, __mod__ (url % query) is an alias for update_query, and comparison operators __eq__/__lt__/__le__/__gt__/__ge__ order by the raw five-tuple.

text: How does yarl keep a scheme-shaped colon in a relative path from turning into a scheme?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:_encode_relative_scheme_colon re-encodes a leading all-scheme-chars run followed by ':' as %3A; encode_url, build, build_pre_encoded_url, from_parts_uncached and human_repr all apply it to scheme-less paths.
